analysis: The only change in this PR is in the test file EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift at line 313 (head). The `recordServerStream` helper's switch now has `.logprobs` added to the `.toolCall, .toolCallDelta` continue case. This looks like an exhaustiveness fix for a new `MLXServerGenerationEvent.logprobs` case. It exists only in the test target, so it adds no production code, no new attack surface, and no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, or data handling. I examined the BASE excerpts (lines 1811-2591) and the HEAD excerpt (lines 1-653). They are test scaffolding with scripted engines and stub tokenizers, and they do not touch real keys, network or disk. The tests cover cacheScope/cacheSalt plumbing (T-041, TB-007), media bypass of the bridge, forged schema metadata rejection, cancellation propagation (T-010), and KV-backend fallback reporting on the heartbeat. The existing assertions remain unchanged and none are weakened. The one uncertainty is outside the supplied evidence: the production `.logprobs` event type and how the server emits it. It is not part of this unit set. Ignoring `.logprobs` in the test recorder does not affect production behavior. I found no regressions and no threat-model gap introduced by this change.
